newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev closes firmer at 507-510 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev closes firmer at 507-510 per dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev rose to 507-510 per dollar at the close from 522-524 in the morning amid rising foreign currency supply in the absence of large dollar buyers from the interbank market, dealers said.
"The lev firmed due to a lack of substantial dollar demand from large clients, low lev liquidity in banks and a rising dollar supply," one dealer said.

Dealers said banks' clients sold dollars because they needed levs for year-end payments while banks had to cover their minimum reserve requirements for November at the central bank by today's deadline.
Uncertainty among traders about the planned introduction of a currency board system in Bulgaria and the exchange rate at which the lev might be pegged also stimulated dollar sales, said dealers.
The central bank continued to buy dollars, as it did last week, in a bid to boost its foreign exchange reserves, traders said. BNB officials were not available for comment.
Traders said the lev might strengthen to 480-500 per dollar in the next couple of days if the central bank did not absorb part of the dollar supply.

Bulgaria is now discussing the introduction of a tight monetary regime called a currency board system under which levs in circulation and banks' minimum reserves at the central bank must be matched by the central bank's forex reserves at a fixed exchange rate.
The central bank's forex reserves fell to $525 million at the end of November from $541 million a month earlier due to its market intervention in support of the lev. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
